doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Steely Dan and L.A. session life
title: Oliver Nelson and not turning down work; Earl Palmer's quote
summary: Asked about doing too many sessions, Scott says he rarely did four a day.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Did you ever get to the point, I’ll preface this by I was able to do an interview with Oliver Nelson Junior.

And he said that his father was afraid to turn down work, that he felt if he started turning down jobs that he, you know, would sink down on the list and consequently he just kept doing it until he couldn’t to it anymore. Did you ever feel like okay I did four sessions today, maybe I should not keep doing that?

Well rarely did I ever, I don’t think I ever did four sessions. The rhythm section guys did. They could work from morning until late at night. That was very, very rare with me. But there were times, in the words of Earl, the great drummer.

Earl Palmer. He said, “You know sometimes it comes to a point when you’re in a session and it just keeps going and going and you go ‘I don’t want to make any more money, I just want to go home.’” And were there some moments like that? Sure. But in the main it was fun to be there. It was really great. As I say, I didn’t work those kind of early in the morning all the way ‘til late at night. I can’t think of one. There may have been a couple but I don’t remember. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
